absent: MMIO write handling, alignment, endianness and behavior for widths other than the four supported sizes.
Flag and register definitions for pending exceptions, control registers and list register fields.
Nested context detection, syndrome layouts and hypervisor control bit positions beyond the observed uses.
Monitor overflow computation, interrupt number allocation and retry behavior on injection failure.
VGIC save, fold, prune, queue and maintenance delivery internals beyond the shown call sites.
Interrupt mapping, configuration, migration and full lifecycle outside deactivation and folding.
Host interrupt chip programming and capability detection for physical deactivation.
Guest halt and resume semantics and configuration lock scope beyond active accesses.

findings.text: MMIO read helper exposes conversion from a caller buffer of one, two, four or eight bytes into a host word result, returning zero for any other length. Single byte loads are direct while wider loads assemble through an intermediate object, with narrower values zero extended.

Pending external abort reporting requires the pending exception marker to be set, otherwise the outcome is negative. For 32-bit guests only undefined and instruction abort and data abort pending kinds affirm, while for 64-bit guests only synchronous and SError pending kinds for the two privileged levels affirm, with every other pending kind negative.

SError injection accepts a virtual CPU plus a syndrome value and always reports success after either delegating, deferring or emulating delivery. A nested SError helper enriches the syndrome with SError class and length indication before delegating to generic nested injection using the SError type.
SError injection requires the virtual CPU mutex to be already held by the caller, checked by an assertion on entry.

Injection selects handling by priority. Nested contexts targeting the upper level use nested injection. Execution at the upper level that cannot receive there stashes the syndrome and arms deferred flag NESTED_SERROR_PENDING. Unmasked conditions pend an emulated exception and record an enriched syndrome in the target level syndrome register. Remaining cases stash only the syndrome portion and set virtual request HCR_VSE in the hypervisor control register.

Exception target is the lower privileged level when nesting is disabled. With nesting, current upper level execution targets the upper level, current lower level targets the lower level, and unprivileged execution targets the upper level only when total trap is set, otherwise the lower level. Any other execution mode is a fatal error.

Syndrome register choice follows the selected target, using the upper register for an upper target and the lower register otherwise. Emulated SError pending likewise chooses between the lower level SError kind and the upper level SError kind based on the same target.
SError is considered masked exactly when the interrupt mask bit in saved processor state is set while the effective non-maskable enhancement is clear.

Effective enhancement is false when the virtual machine lacks the control feature, and false in nested context without the hypervisor enable for that control. Otherwise it reflects the addressed bit from the control register belonging to the selected exception target.

Nested SError target is the upper level for hypervisor context or when asynchronous routing to the upper level is set. Without trap mask enhancement the target is otherwise the lower level. With that enhancement, privileged execution consults the mask bit while unprivileged execution consults overall masking. At the upper level, delivery is impossible unless total trap or asynchronous routing is set.

Nested flush and sync hooks do nothing without nesting support. Flush drains the deferred flag into injection using the stashed syndrome. Sync first reaps the virtual request bit from the hypervisor control register into the deferred flag, then retries injection, allowing changed deliverability such as wakeup conditions to take effect.

Deferred SError state moves between control register request, in-memory pending flag and active injection attempt. Either representation records intent, flush and sync atomically clear the flag while invoking injection, and injection may re-arm either representation according to current masking and target.

Performance monitor flush and sync both refresh monitor state. Refresh does nothing without an in-kernel interrupt controller, otherwise it drives the monitor interrupt with current overflow status as the level.

VGIC synchronization first handles version three nesting: nested state performs nested synchronization and returns, while capable but non-nested state refreshes the maintenance interrupt. It then saves distributive state when kernel access is permitted, folds state, and prunes the active list on all versions except version five.

Nested synchronization walks mapped list registers and merges host state bits into shadow copies while preserving remaining fields. Hardware entries that were valid before the run but invalid after trigger emulated deactivation using the physical identifier. It then copies virtual machine control and enable count state from hardware, clears hardware control, enforces ordering, and refreshes the maintenance interrupt.
Shadow index for a guest list position equals the count of mapped positions below it, packing sparse guest numbering into dense host numbering.

Maintenance level is asserted only when the interface is enabled and the computed status word is nonzero. The status aggregates end of interrupt, underflow when at most one entry remains with underflow enabled, list empty and no pending indications gated by their enables and counts, and group enable and disable transitions observed through virtual machine control.

Maintenance aggregates scan every list register to build an end mask, an empty mask and a global pending indication. End indication requires cleared state with request set, with one variant additionally requiring cleared hardware association and the other requiring cleared hardware bit.
Host list register accessor selects among sixteen hardware entries using the low four bits of the supplied index, treating any other selection as unreachable.

Deactivation ignores requests outside end of interrupt mode one or beyond the private plus shared range. It separates the CPU identifier from the interrupt number with special handling for version two software interrupts. Under disabled interrupts it takes no action for unqueued interrupts, falls back to clear active handling for interrupts resident in a list register, and otherwise synthesizes a list value with active cleared after validating the source identifier. It then conditionally clears physical state, folds the value and requests pruning on the owning CPU.

Deactivation executes with local interrupts saved and holds the per-interrupt lock while inspecting ownership and residency. Folding holds the same per-interrupt lock while merging state. The clear active memory mapped path holds the configuration mutex across prepare, per-bit update and finish.

Active transitions use interrupt saving acquisition of the per-interrupt lock, queuing the interrupt when activating and releasing otherwise. Version three accesses from a different CPU and any shared interrupt access halt the guest before the update and resume it afterwards.

Descriptor vgic_irq carries identity and host mapping, edge or level configuration, software active and pending latches and physical line level, source set and active source, list residency and owning CPU, host number and a dedicated lock. Interface state vgic_v3_cpu_if carries virtual machine control. Aggregate mi_state carries end mask plus empty mask plus pending flag. Shadow state shadow_if carries a register map.

Clear active decoding converts the access address at one bit granularity into a base interrupt number, then iterates over set bits in the written value to clear each successive interrupt and release its reference.

Folding resolves the interrupt from the virtual identifier, honoring model specific width and software interrupt handling, and ignores unmapped entries. Under lock it merges active state except for low power interrupts, latches edge pending, clears level soft pending on empty state, records source identifiers for version two software interrupts, handles resampling and clears residency. Level shared interrupts that signal end of interrupt notify completion and decrement the active shared count.

Resampling applies only to level configured hardware mapped interrupts. It samples the physical line when resampling is required and neither active nor latched, or when pending or deactivated with line high, and it clears physical active when the sampled line is low.

Physical active control requires hardware mapping and forwards the request to the host chip. Physical deactivation uses a legacy instruction path on one capability and a direct write path otherwise. Hardware active updates from user access are ignored, while other updates set software active and forward to hardware.

Fatal handling covers unknown execution modes, missing hardware mapping when programming physical state, and invalid list register selection. Warning handling covers missing interrupt descriptors during deactivation and failures while injecting the monitor interrupt.

In nested state, physical deactivation is skipped for hardware associated synthesized values to avoid errata that could break delivery of the highest pending interrupt. Hardware software interrupts clear active without tracking, and user space updates to hardware active state are dropped.

Supported MMIO widths are one, two, four and eight bytes. Host provides sixteen list registers addressed by four index bits. Deactivation carries the software source identifier in bits twelve through ten. Clear active decoding uses single bit granularity.
